claims.text: The rear wheel turns (chainring teeth ÷ cog teeth) times per pedal revolution.
A derailleur moves the chain from one sprocket to another.
Penny-farthings had their pedals attached directly to a large front wheel.
John Kemp Starley's Rover of 1885 is widely regarded as the first successful chain-driven safety bicycle.
Near the summit of Mount Everest, water boils at roughly 70 °C.
Turning water into vapour at its boiling point takes about 2,260 kJ of energy per kilogram.
Many electric kettles switch off using a bimetallic thermostat that senses steam.
The Russell Hobbs K1 of 1955 is credited as the first automatic electric kettle.
Control (false): the first automatic kettle was released in 1925.
Photosynthesis turns carbon dioxide and water into sugar and oxygen using light.
Chlorophyll absorbs mainly blue and red light and reflects green light.
In van Helmont's willow experiment the tree gained about 74 kg over five years while the soil lost about 57 g.
Priestley (1771) found plants restore air used up by a candle, and Ingenhousz (1779) found this needs light.
